mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 1.75% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be negative due to expectations of persistent tightening and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the pre-tightening average (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS drops below 1.75 for three consecutive months without a subsequent reversal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS < previous + > 10,000) predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as labor market weakness outweighs wage growth momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous + 10,000 and PAYEMS < PAYEMS[-1] + 10,000 within the same month
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the 20-day forward return is positive in at least 70% of such labor market signal events, or the interaction term (PAYEMS + lagged PAYEMS) fails to explain more than 5% of the forward return variance.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows faster than consumer demand proxies (HOUST), the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive as supply-side expansion creates excess capacity and reduces growth risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > HOUST growth rate over the preceding month
failure_condition: In a 200-day window, the interaction of INDPRO-HOUST does not explain more than 15% of the 60-day forward return variance, or the 60-day forward return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 252 for three consecutive months signals disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as rate-cut expectations rise.
failure_condition: Over 100 such months, the 20-day forward return is never positive when the CPIAUCSL condition is met, or the average return under the condition is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% followed by sustained levels above 4.2% for two months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return due to heightened recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4% and UNRATE > 4.2 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20 such episodes, the 5-day forward return is not negative in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not statistically lower than during pre-recession baselines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly real personal consumption expenditures (implied via GDPC1) grows faster than GDP (INDPRO) for two consecutive quarters, the S&P 20-day forward return is positive as it signals healthy demand growth not yet fully priced in.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > INDPRO growth rate for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: Across 40 such quarters, the interaction does not explain more than 10% of the 20-day forward return variance, or the average forward return under the condition is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in retail sales proxies (not directly available in the catalog; fallback: HOUST as a demand proxy) followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market interprets the bounce as stabilization.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST[-1] and HOUST[-2] < HOUST[-1] within the same month
failure_condition: In 50 such recovery events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the interaction with a 3-month moving average of HOUST fails to improve model fit by 5% AICc.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat for three consecutive months while consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) continues to decline, the S&P 20-day forward return is negative due to persistent supply-side stagnation and deflationary expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO flat for three consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 40 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.05), or the interaction term does not explain more than 8% of the return variance.
